Yes, in one respect. I edited `tests/test_game.py`, which is in my allowed files, to add an autouse fixture. It patches `normalize_word`, `is_valid_word`, `get_random_word` and `score_guess` inside `wordle.game`, because the real `words.py` and `scorer.py` are still stubs that raise `NotImplementedError`. The patched `is_valid_word` returns True for everything, and the patched `score_guess` is a simplified HIT/MISS comparison. So the local 7/7 pass shows the game's state logic works. It doesn't show that my code works with the real dictionary or scorer.

I did not special-case any test inputs in `game.py`. It has no hardcoded words and no branches keyed to the test data. I didn't touch config or shared files.

The remaining risk is the one I flagged earlier. `make_guess` rejects any word the real `is_valid_word` says isn't in the dictionary. If the real word list lacks `WRONG`, `WORLD` or `GREAT`, those tests would fail in the validator once the mocks are gone. I haven't checked that.
